title: Scope of Work: Supply/Service - Technical Description/Requirement /Quality requirement
body:
For Supplies:
The Stores supplied shall be of the best quality and Workmanship shall be in strict conformity with all the drawings and specifications furnished with the Purchase Orders/Contract schedule/Development schedule and shall address the Technical description in all respects. In case if tenders are called for in accordance with `particulars', then the SUPPLIER to supply in accordance with such `particulars', which shall be deemed to be an admission on his part that he has fully acquainted himself with the details thereof and no claim on his part which may arise on account of no examination or insufficient examination of the `particulars' will in any circumstances be considered.  The items not specifically listed but required for completeness of stores / system/ Development deemed to be included. All supplies should be accompanied by SUPPLIER’s work inspections/test certificates duly certifying, that the Stores are in strict conformity with the drawings/ specifications.  The final acceptance will be subject to inspection and approval at BUYER's premises. Once the stores are rejected and communicated to the SUPPLIER, no request shall be entertained for re-inspection or acceptance of the stores. However, BUYER reserves the right to re-inspect the stores and consider acceptance at his discretion

title: Price Variation
body:
The PO or Contract is on firm price basis, except otherwise it is specifically agreed herein for escalation or on price rulings at the time of despatch and its admissibility is accepted. It is specifically agreed that the below formula for determining the quantum of escalation admissible with reference to a fixed base period and price ruling at that period shall be taken as a base for deciding the escalations.
It is agreed that base period and prices shall be on mutually agreed terms, supported with necessary documentary evidence. The claim shall be supported with necessary documentary evidence, as compared to the base prices for admitting the escalation claims. Applicability of escalation shall be up to point of ordering (or) point of delivery need as agreed. The escalation is calculated on year to year basis or point to point basis. Methodology of calculation of escalation is specified as below:
P    = Po {(A + B(L/Lo)+ C (M/Mo)}
P    = Final price payable in the year of delivery
Po = The base price at _ (year) economic conditions
Lo = Average Labour Index of the base   _ (year)
Mo = Average Material Index of the base   _ (year)
L   = Average Labour Index …….. Months prior to date of delivery (as applicable at SUPPLIER's country/as  per supplier quotation).
M   = Average Material Index …….. Months prior to date of delivery (as applicable at SUPPLIER's country/ as per Supplier quotation).
A, B & C = Percentages corresponding to fixed elements, labour and material respectively. Escalation cap (+/-) applicable (percentage) with the above price variation formula to be indicated.
The indices incorporated in the escalation formula should be Govt. Published/ in public domain and capable of being verified.
Escalation/Revision in price shall not be admitted for the delayed supplies i.e. beyond the original contract period.

title: Packing Conditions
body:
The stores should be properly packed for tropical storage and for transport by rail, road, sea or air so as to ensure and to protect them against loss, damage, corrosion in transit on arrival at their destination. The packing and marking of packages shall be done by and at the expense of the SUPPLIER. Each package shall contain a Packing Note quoting Purchase Order number and date showing its contents in detail. Each package shall be properly marked with Purchase Order No., Consignee’s name & address, gross weight, package-handling instructions etc. The package shall have adequate provision for handling during transit and at destination.
The packing, shipping, storage and processing of the delivery must comply with the prevailing legislation and regulations concerning safety, the environment and working conditions. In case of Imports, items packed with raw/ solid wood packing material should be treated as per ISPM – 15 (fumigation) and accompanied by Phytosanitory/ Fumigation certificate. If safety information sheets exist for a delivery or the packaging, the SUPPLIER must always supply these sheets direct (at the same time). The packing shall allow for easy removal and checking of goods on receipt and comply with carrier’s conditions of packing or established trade practices.  If any consignment needs special handling instruction, the same shall be clearly marked with standard symbols / instructions. Hazardous material should be notified as such and their packing, transportation and other protection must conform to relevant regulations

title: Inspection and Technical document requirements
body:
The supply made against respective orders will be subject to BUYER inspection at his premises. The SUPPLIER shall be responsible for items supplied till the same have been inspected and accepted by BUYER. If required on case to case basis, the Buyer shall conduct the inspection along with the certifying agencies such as RCMA, CEMILAC, CRI, CRE or any relevant agency etc. for acceptance.
In case the goods/services are rejected at the time of inspection at BUYER’s place or the rejections are noticed at the time of further processing the SUPPLIER will be informed of these rejections.  On receipt of this information the SUPPLIER shall immediately arrange to collect the rejected items at his cost and risk and arrange for the replacement of goods within the shortest possible time. Under no circumstances the SUPPLIER shall compel the BUYER to rework the rejected goods.  The rejected material will lie at BUYER’s premises at the risk and cost of the SUPPLIER, pending receipt of disposal instruction from them. If so desired by the SUPPLIER, the rejected materials, for which no payment made by BUYER may be packed and returned to the SUPPLIER for arranging replacement/rectification on ‘freight to pay’ basis at his cost and risk and the dispatch documents will be forwarded to the SUPPLIER directly by BUYER to enable him to arrange insurance and take delivery of the same. Wherever payment is already made by BUYER to the SUPPLIER, the rejected material will be returned to the SUPPLIER against refund of the amount already paid by BUYER / submission of BG or Credit Note or the refund amount shall be adjusted against pending orders/pending payments of ordering Division or any HAL Divisions to the extent of the value of rejected goods only. The packing, freight charges etc., on replacement of returned materials shall be borne by the SUPPLIER irrespective of the terms in the purchase order, since such charges were already incurred and borne by BUYER on the original consignment, which got rejected and returned to the SUPPLIER. In case the rejected materials are not required to be replaced, freight, insurance charges etc., incurred by BUYER on the original consignment shall be recovered from the SUPPLIER's bills. In case, no disposal instructions are received from the SUPPLIER, regarding rejected stores, as contemplated above, or where the amount due from the SUPPLIER, cannot be recovered from the pending supplies, within 3 months, from the date of intimation to the SUPPLIER, then the BUYER reserves the right to dispose the rejected stores, in the manner BUYER deems fit. Under the given circumstances appropriate amount will be recovered from the SUPPLIER, along with cost of disposal. If any balance amount is receivable /refundable, the same will be recovered from any pending dues of the SUPPLIER from any office/division of the BUYER.
BUYER or his authorized representative shall be entitled at all reasonable times during execution to inspect, examine and test at the SUPPLIER's premises the material and workmanship of all stores to be supplied under the Contract, and if the part of the stores are being manufactured at other premises the SUPPLIER shall obtain BUYER's or his authorized representative’s concurrence to inspect, examine and test as if the said stores are being manufactured at the SUPPLIER’s premises. Such inspection, examination and testing, if made shall not release the SUPPLIER from any obligation under the Contract.  If the defects are not remedied within a reasonable/stipulated time, the BUYER may proceed to rectify the defects at the SUPPLIER’s risk & cost but without prejudice to any other rights which the BUYER may have against the SUPPLIER in respect of their failure to remedy such defects. All costs related to inspections and re-inspections shall be borne by the SUPPLIER. The cost of inspection staff/ third party specified by the BUYER shall be borne by BUYER, unless otherwise specifically agreed. When the Contract provides for tests on the premises of the SUPPLIER or any of his Sub-contractor/s, SUPPLIER shall be responsible to provide assistance such as, labour, materials, electricity, fuels, stores, apparatus, instruments as may be required and as may be reasonably demanded to carry out such tests efficiently. Cost of any type test or such other special tests shall be borne by the BUYER only if specifically agreed. The SUPPLIER shall give the authorized representative of the BUYER reasonable prior notice in writing of the date on and the place at which any stores will be ready for inspection/ testing as provided in the Contract.

title: Warranty
body:
Period of Warranty:
All the Stores supplied shall be warranted against any defect in material, workmanship, defective design, materials and non-conformance to intended performance, manufacturing defects, or dimension etc., generally for a period of 12 calendar months from the date of satisfactory installation, commissioning and acceptance of the equipment/supplies/work or 18 calendar months from the date of delivery and acceptance of supply at BUYER's place / BUYER's designated place, whichever is earlier.
Obligations of SUPPLIER during warranty:
The SUPPLIER shall remedy such defects at its own cost or replace free of charge such stores when called upon to do so.
The SUPPLIER cannot absolve its responsibility for warranty of material even though it is inspected & approved by its Inspection authority.
During warranty minimum uptime of 95%(wherever applicable)shall be ensured failing which warranty period shall be deemed to be proportionately extended.
In case of defective Stores which need to be re-exported for repairs to the manufacturer’s works, to &fro freight, insurance charges & custom duty/charges for replacement have to be borne by the SUPPLIER.
During warranty period any equipment or component thereof supplied by the SUPPLIER, suffers due to defective material and or due to improper design and or due to defective drawing or due to faulty workmanship the SUPPLIER will assume full responsibility of rectification of such defective equipment or component thereof including direct expenses related to removal and re-positioning of the replacement/repaired equipment or component thereof and subsequent test & trial, incurred thereon without any financial implication to BUYER.
The SUPPLIER shall be responsible for payment of custom duty/charges if applicable for replaced part/equipment.
Warranty calls needs to be attended within 48 hrs. Warranty of the stores will be extended by residual period of warranty.
Remedies during Warranty:
If the defects intimated during the Warranty period are not remedied within a reasonable/stipulated time, the BUYER may proceed to rectify the defects at the SUPPLIER's risk and cost, but without prejudice to any other rights which the BUYER may have against the SUPPLIER in respect of the failure of the SUPPLIER to remedy such defects.
In the event of SUPPLIER’s failure to attend the Warranty defects within a reasonable period of time, the Performance Bank Guarantee will be en-cashed by the BUYER. The BUYER’s decision shall be final and binding on SUPPLIER in this regard.
All packing, forwarding, insurance and delivery charges arising against this would be borne by the SUPPLIER. The warrantee period would be extended by equivalent period for which the material is not available for the repaired parts, which were repaired & replaced during the Warranty period. The Warranty is subject to proper preservation, maintenance, storage, handling and usage of equipment by BUYER/BUYER's end customer and does not cover repairs carried out without the prior consent of the SUPPLIER / SUPPLIER’s representative.
In the event BUYER desires to have extension of Warranty period beyond the stipulated period, as above, the SUPPLIER shall quote for the same (on monthly /annual basis) for the period of such extension.

title: Product Support
body:
The SUPPLIER should agree to provide product support for the equipment supplied, assemblies/ sub-assemblies, fitment items and consumables, Special Maintenance Tools (SMT) / Special Test Equipment’s (STE) subcontracted from other agencies / manufacturer by the SUPPLIER, by making available spare parts, components & tools etc., accessories of equipment and services for a minimum period of _____ years from the date of supply.
SUPPLIER should supply recommended spares for operator level servicing and should carry out necessary product support activities. SUPPLIER should also recommend a list of test equipment/ fixtures and special tools required for servicing at _______/ its customer bases.  SUPPLIER will extend need based technical assistance to the BUYER for maintenance of the product/ System during the warranty period. SUPPLIER shall provide an effective Product Support and maintenance services on demand from the BUYER and at mutually agreed financial consideration, for mutually agreed period from the date of supply of the product/ System. Product Support covers the following areas:
- Spares Support
- Field Support
- Maintenance Support

MAINTENANCE SUPPORT:
SUPPLIER shall carry out scheduled, periodic and unscheduled maintenance and snag rectification and for this purpose maintenance personnel will be deputed at mutually agreed terms and conditions.
In case of prices for long-term supplies of spare parts or price catalogue are not available/ applicable, provision for entering into long term business agreements on supply, servicing and repairs like LTSA / LTRA should be provided by SUPPLIER in the scope of the contract till establishment of Repair Overhaul Facility at HAL  or in India. The SUPPLIER agrees to undertake Maintenance Contract for a maximum period of ______ months, extendable till the complete Engineering Support Package which will be provided by the SUPPLIER. In the event of any obsolescence during the above mentioned period of product support in respect of any component or sub-system, mutual consultation between the SUPPLIER and BUYER will be undertaken to arrive at an acceptable solution including additional cost, if any. Any improvement /modification / up gradation by the SUPPLIER or their sub-suppliers on the stores / equipment being purchased under the Contract will be communicated by the SUPPLIER to the BUYER and, if required by the BUYER, these will be carried out by the SUPPLIER at BUYER's cost. The SUPPLIER agrees to provide an Engineering Support Package as modified after confirmatory Maintenance Evaluation Trials (METs). The SUPPLIER agrees to undertake the repair and maintenance of the equipment, SMTs/STEs test set up, assemblies / sub-assemblies and stores supplied under this contract for a period of _____ years as maintenance contract as specified or provision of complete Engineering Support Package to the BUYER whichever is later, as per terms and conditions mutually agreed between the SUPPLIER and the BUYER

title: Liquidated Damages
body: The time for and the date of delivery of the stores/completion of work stipulated in the Purchase Order shall be deemed to be the essence of the contract, and delivery/work must be completed no later than the dates specified therein. Should the SUPPLIER fail to deliver the material to HAL premises/designated place or complete the work or any consignment thereof, within the period prescribed for such delivery/work, BUYER shall be entitled to recover from the SUPPLIER agreed liquidated damages, and not by way of penalty a sum of 0.5% per week of delay or part thereof, subject to a maximum of 10% as our claim towards liquidated damages on the undelivered part of the order/scope of work. The LD will be charged on the value of the purchase order including statutory levies, freight and insurance wherever not included in the price.  Imposition, recovery or settlement of this LD shall not affect BUYER's right to performance, compensation and termination of the Contract/agreement.

body:

body:

title: Suspension of Work
body:
BUYER may, by a written order, instruct the SUPPLIER to suspend the work or any part of the work for the period and in the manner which BUYER considers necessary.  The SUPPLIER shall cease to work on said part of the work on the effective date of suspension, but shall continue to perform such unsuspended part of the work, if any.  During the suspension, the SUPPLIER shall properly protect and secure the work so far as is necessary in the opinion of BUYER.
BUYER shall not pay any costs incurred by the SUPPLIER in giving effect to the suspension order, including under the following:
necessary because of Force Majeure; or
necessary for the proper execution of the work, or any part thereof; or
necessary because of some negligence, error or other default on the part of the  SUPPLIER; or
necessary for the health or safety of BUYER and/or SUPPLIER Personnel, third parties or for the protection of the work, BUYER property or environment; or
Otherwise provided for in the Contract.
If the suspension of the work is not attributable to any negligence, error or default of the SUPPLIER, in the opinion of BUYER, and should be of such duration as to entitle the SUPPLIER in BUYER's reasonable judgment to an extension of the completion date, the parties shall negotiate such extension. However, there shall be no variation to the Contract Price payable to the SUPPLIER.
If the suspension of the work is not attributable due to any negligence, error or default of the SUPPLIER and except under Force Majeure circumstances, maximum period for suspension shall be as defined for Go-Live deferment under clause_____________ (as per FM clause).
BUYER may, at any time, authorize resumption of the suspended part of the work by notifying the SUPPLIER of the part of the work to be resumed and the effective date of withdrawal of the suspension.  The work shall be promptly resumed by the SUPPLIER after receipt of such notification.

title: Termination
body:
BUYER reserves the right to cancel the order/contract with 15 days’ prior notice without any financial liability in the event of any of the following:
When the item offered by the SUPPLIER repeatedly fails in the inspection and/or the SUPPLIER is not in a position to either rectify the defects as stipulated in the warranty or offer items conforming to the contracted quality standards.
When the SUPPLIER fails to honour any part of the contract including failure to deliver the contracted stores/render services in time.

title: Intellectual Property Rights
body:
General IPR clause:
If any Patent design, trademark, copyright or any other intellectual property rights apply to the delivery or accompanying documentation, BUYER shall be entitled to the legal use thereof free of charge by means of a non-exclusive, worldwide, perpetual license. All intellectual property rights that arise due to the execution of the delivery by the SUPPLIER and by its employees or third parties involved by the SUPPLIER for performance of the agreement belong to BUYER.
The SUPPLIER shall be obligated to do everything necessary to obtain or establish the above mentioned rights.  The SUPPLIER guarantees that the delivery does not infringe on any of the intellectual property rights of third parties. The SUPPLIER shall also be obligated to do everything necessary to obtain or establish the alternate acceptable arrangement pending resolution of any (alleged) claims by third parties. The SUPPLIER shall indemnify the BUYER against any (alleged) claims by third parties in this regard and shall reimburse BUYER for any damages suffered as a result thereof.
Indemnity against third party IPR claims:
1.1  The SUPPLIER shall, subject to the BUYER’s compliance with paragraph 22.1.3 below, indemnify and hold harmless the BUYER, its employees and officers from and against any and all suits, actions or proceedings, claims, demands, losses, damages, costs and expenses, including reasonable attorney’s fees, which the BUYER suffers as a result of any infringement or alleged infringement of any patent, utility  model, registered design, trademark, copy right or other intellectual property right of third parties registered or otherwise existing at the date of the contract by reason of the performance of the works by the SUPPLIER or use of the same in the country where the works is located or carried on or sold.
1.2    Such indemnity shall not cover any use of (part of) the works other than for the purpose specified in the contract or not in accordance with the SUPPLIER’s instructions, any modification of the works by the BUYER not agreed with SUPPLIER, any infringement arising from the use of the works in combination with any other equipment, plant or material not supplied by SUPPLIER or from any design, data, drawing, specification or other document provided or designed by the BUYER.
1.3    If any proceedings are brought or any claim is made against the BUYER as per above para-22.1.1, the BUYER shall promptly notify the SUPPLIER thereof in writing. The SUPPLIER shall be entitled to conduct at its own expense and sole discretion such proceedings or claim and any negotiations for the settlement of the same. The SUPPLIER shall not make any admission that may be prejudicial to the defence of any such proceedings or claim. The BUYER shall, at the SUPPLIER’s request, provide all reasonable assistance to the SUPPLIER in conducting such proceedings or claim and shall be reimbursed by the SUPPLIER for all reasonable expenses incurred thereby.
1.4   In the event of any actual or alleged infringement under this clause the SUPPLIER shall have the option at its own expense, to modify or replace or obtain a licence to use any infringing part/s of the scope of work so that there is no further infringement.
IPR clause for outsourcing works:
1.1 In case of any  design, data, drawing, specification or other document /details provided by HAL to Contractor  having exclusive Patent design, trademark, copyright or any other intellectual property rights over such material under delivery or accompanying documentation, then the Contractor  outsourcing Vendor/Developer shall be entitled to legal use thereof  particularly and specifically for the purpose of execution of the scope of work as stated in the outsourcing contract to carry out the  process or procedure for achieving the required output for  fulfilling the objective of the outsourcing contract and. The Contractor’s Vendor/Developer shall not have any legal right or legal claim over the Intellectual Property Right etc against the drawings/technical documentation/ processes/ deliverables/ services/development etc that is delivered back to HAL as a final product arising out during execution of the said outsourcing contract and the same shall be in the name of HAL as a perpetual entity having Intellectual Property Rights.
1.2 The processes, documentation and drawings etc produced by Contractor during the course of Contract execution shall be released in favour of ‘HAL’ and HAL has sole and full rights to use it at any point of time and share with any third party for its business purposes/execution of contract purposes etc, and Contractor shall not have any rights to claim IPR etc over the same and shall not use such data/information/drawings etc for any purposes without HAL prior permission. Contractor shall not be permitted to deal with HAL customers/any third party for such items/services. "

title: Exit criteria
body:
(a) Exit Clause in a contract, when HAL is Supplier, Service Provider / Facilitator:
In the event HAL is a Supplier:
In case if there is any change in Buyer requirements be it for any reason during the currency of the contract, leading to cancellation of contract with Supplier and by such act/omission if the Supplier incurs such amounts for establishing Buyer’s  requirements for execution of that contract or places required purchase orders with its vendors for complying the contract requirements, then the Buyer need to make good the loss/expenses incurred by Supplier  for compliance with the Contract requirements, subject to such claim (loss/expenses) is substantiated with the supportive documents/proof.
In the event HAL is a Service Provider/Facilitator:
In case if there is any change in Customer requirements be it for any reason during the currency of the contract, leading to cancellation of contract with Service Provider/Facilitator and by such act/omission if the Service Provider/Facilitator incurs such amounts for establishing Customer’s requirements for execution of that contract or places required purchase orders with its vendors for complying the contract requirements, then the Customer need to make good the loss/expenses incurred by Service Provider/Facilitator for compliance with the Contract requirements, subject to such claim (loss/expenses) is substantiated with the supportive documents/proof.
(b) Exit Clause in a Contract when HAL is a Buyer:
The contract/order may be terminated under the following circumstances:
a. In the event of unsatisfactory performance by the SUPPLIER during the contract period, or any of the information provided by the SUPPLIER is found to be untrue, or SUPPLIER is found to have attempted to influence any person involved with the contract through unethical means, the contract shall be terminated with -------- months advance notice without any financial implication to BUYER. Notwithstanding the foregoing, in cases where it is found that a SUPPLIER is engaged in unethical practices, the same shall be barred from participating in the future contracts for a period of __ years.
b. If there is change in BUYER requirement, contract shall be terminated with ------ months advance notice. The liability of BUYER in this case will be agreed mutually (in any case, it shall be proportionate to the expenditure incurred by SUPPLIER till date of issuing Termination Notice and shall not exceed contract value). In the event of termination of contract by either party, then the SUPPLIER shall ensure the following:
IPR’s are transferred to BUYER to enable BUYER to proceed on the work with other SUPPLIER. SUPPLIER also will render all assistance till the other SUPPLIER fully take over the balance work.
Transfer title and deliver all or any part thereof of the supplies, materials, work-in-progress, finished Products, Tooling, drawings and data produced or acquired by SUPPLIER specifically for the Product/work being terminated.
Supply of products and its components / spares at least for a period of ___ years from the date of such termination.
c. The SUPPLIER is declared bankrupt or becomes insolvent.
d. The delivery of material is delayed due to causes of Force Majeure by more than (________ months).
e. Based on the decision of the Arbitration Tribunal.

title: Confidentiality
body:
1. This Contract and its Annexures shall be treated as confidential by the Parties and their officers and employees.
2. Unless otherwise specified herein, neither Party or any of their affiliated companies shall make any news release, public announcement, advertisement, denial or confirmation, disclose of some or any part of this Contract or transactions contemplated under this Contract/Agreement/Order to any third party without the prior written consent of the other Party
3. The Party disclosing information is termed as Disclosing Party and the Party receiving information is termed as Receiving Party, Each Party undertakes:
to keep the other Party's Confidential Information confidential using the same degree of care as the receiving Party uses to protect its own Proprietary Information against public disclosure but in no case any less degree than reasonable care; and
not to make any disclosure of the other Party's Confidential Information to any third party and to use the same only for the Purpose; and
not to make any copies of the other Party's Confidential Information, or translation or transfer of the same to other documents or media nor to disseminate the same within its own organisation save as is strictly necessary for the Purpose; and not to assign the rights and obligations of the Parties without their prior written consent thereto.
4. Provided, however, that the foregoing restrictions and obligations shall not apply to any information which it can be shown:
is already or hereafter becomes published otherwise than through the fault or negligence of the receiving Party; or
is lawfully obtained by the recipient from a third party  having rights to disclose to the receiving Party, without restrictions as to use or disclosure, or
is already known to the receiving Party at the date of receipt of the information pursuant to this Contract/Agreement/Order, or
is independently developed by the receiving Party.
is required to be disclosed under any law, judicial order or Government order or regulation provided receiving Party gives disclosing Party  timely notice, where possible, of the contemplated disclosure so as to give the disclosing Party an opportunity to intervene to preserve the confidentiality of the information. Or such disclosure is limited to those persons to whom the Receiving Party is legally compelled to disclose the information to; and
5. The technical information provided by SUPPLIER under this Contract shall be treated as confidential by the BUYER and shall be used by BUYER only for purpose intended and shall not be disclosed to any third party.
6. The provisions of this clause shall survive and remain in force notwithstanding the termination or expiry of this Contract.
7. The BUYER shall limit access of technical documentation being provided under this Contract only to such of its employees involved in relevant operations concerning the equipment on a need to know basis.
8. Non-adherence to this Clause by the SUPPLIER shall be treated, amongst others, as a material breach of this Contract.

title: Fall clause
body: The price quoted shall be in no event exceed the lowest price at which the SUPPLIER sell the stores or offer to sell stores of identical description to any person(s)/organization originating Internationally or within India including the purchases by any department of the Govt. of India, the State Govt. or any statutory undertaking of the Govt. of India / State Govt., as the case may be during the period till the completion of the performance or currency of the present Contract. If at any time during the said period, the SUPPLIER reduces the sales price, sells or offers to sell such stores to any person/ organization including BUYER or any department of Central Govt. or any Dept. of State Govt., or any statutory undertaking of the Central or State Govt., of Government of India or Foreign Government  as the case may be at a price lower than the price chargeable under the contract, then the SUPPLIER shall forthwith notify such reduction/sale or offer to sale to BUYER and the price payable under the contract  for the stores supplied after the date of coming into force of such reduction or sale or offer to sale shall stand correspondingly reduced with due allowance for quantities and intervening time period.

title: Arbitration
body:
Clause for Indigenous SUPPLIERs/Executants:
Any dispute or difference whatsoever arising between the parties out of or relating to the construction, meaning, scope, operation or effect of this contract or the validity or the breach thereof shall be settled by bilateral discussions.
Any dispute or difference whatsoever arising between the parties out of or relating to the construction, meaning, scope, operation or effect of this contract or the validity or the breach thereof, which cannot be settled amicably within sixty (60) days or such longer period as may be mutually agreed upon, from the date on which either party informs the other in writing by a notice that such dispute, disagreement or question exists, shall be settled by arbitration.
The Arbitration Proceedings shall be conducted in India under the Indian Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 and its subsequent amendments from time to time. The award of such Arbitration shall be enforceable in Indian Courts only. The law applicable to arbitration shall be Indian law.
The arbitration tribunal shall be consisting of sole arbitrator (is it not only one in all cases.  The sole arbitrator shall be nominated by the parties within ninety (90) days of the receipt of the notice mentioned above through mutual discussions, failing which the arbitrator shall be nominated under the provision of Indian Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 at the request of either party or by dispute resolution institutions like Indian Council of Arbitration or ICADR, but said nomination would be after consultation with both the parties. The award of the arbitration shall be final and binding on the parties to this contract.
Both Parties if agree for an Arbitration Tribunal consisting of three Arbitrators, then out of three Arbitrators two Arbitrators shall be appointed by each party to the Contract and the so appointed two Arbitrators shall jointly appoint the third Arbitrator who shall be the Presiding officer.
In the event of a vacancy caused in the office of the arbitrator, the party/parties which/who nominated such arbitrator shall be entitled to nominate another in the place of retiring/outgoing Arbitrator and the arbitration proceedings shall continue from the stage they were left by the retiring arbitrator.
In the event of both  parties failing to nominate arbitrator within sixty (60) days after the  place of arbitrator falling vacant, then the other party(proposing party) shall be entitled after due notice of at least thirty (30) days to request dispute resolution institutions in India like Indian Council of Arbitration  or  ICADR to nominate another arbitrator as above.
The language(s) of the arbitration shall be English. “Except as may be required by law, neither a party nor its representatives may disclose the existence, content, or results of any arbitration hereunder without the prior written consent of (all/both) parties.”
In case of technical disputes involving confidential matters, the issue shall be referred to a high level technical authority for each party, appointed for this purpose.
Clause for Foreign Supplier/Executants:
Any dispute or difference whatsoever arising between the parties out of or relating to the construction, meaning, scope, operation or effect of this contract or the validity or the breach thereof shall be settled by bilateral discussions.
Any dispute or difference whatsoever arising between the parties out of or relating to the construction, meaning, scope, operation or effect of this contract or the validity or the breach thereof, which cannot be settled amicably within sixty (60) days or such longer period as may be mutually agreed upon, from the date on which either party informs the other in writing by a notice that such dispute, disagreement or question exists, shall be settled by Arbitration.
The Arbitration Proceedings shall be conducted in India under the Indian Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 and its subsequent amendments from time to time. The award of such Arbitration shall be enforceable in Indian Courts only. The law applicable to conducting arbitration shall be Indian law.  (Indian law or foreign law to be negotiated and decided by the parties to contract and need to modify accordingly).
The arbitration tribunal shall be consisting of sole arbitrator. The arbitrator, who shall not be a citizen or domicile of the country of either of the parties or of any other country unacceptable to any of the parties, shall be nominated by the parties within ninety (90) days of the receipt of the notice mentioned above, failing which the arbitrator may be nominated under the provisions of Indian Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 or by dispute resolution institutions like Indian Council of Arbitration and ICADR. In case, nomination of sole arbitrator under Indian Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 or by dispute resolution institutions like ICA and ICADR are not acceptable to the SUPPLIER, then the sole arbitrator may be nominated by the President of International Chamber of Commerce, Paris, but the said nomination would be after consultation with both the parties and shall preclude any citizen with domicile of any country as mentioned above.
Both Parties if agree for an Arbitration Tribunal consisting of three Arbitrators, then out of three Arbitrators two Arbitrators shall be appointed by each party to the Contract and the so appointed two Arbitrators shall jointly appoint the third Arbitrator who shall be the Presiding officer.
The Arbitration Tribunal shall have its seat at Bangalore in India or any suitable place in India as may be decided by the arbitrator. The award of the Arbitration shall be final and binding on the parties to this contract.
Each party shall bear its own cost of preparing and presenting its case. The cost of Arbitration including the fees and expenses of the arbitrator shall be shared equally by the SUPPLIER and the BUYER, unless otherwise awarded by the Arbitration Tribunal.
In the event of a vacancy caused in the office of the arbitrator, the party/parties which/who nominated such arbitrator shall be entitled to nominate another in the place of retiring/outgoing Arbitrator and the arbitration proceedings shall continue from the stage they were left by the retiring/outgoing arbitrator.
In the event of both  parties failing to nominate arbitrator within sixty (60) days, after the  place of arbitrator falling vacant, then the other party(proposing party) shall be entitled after due notice of at least thirty (30) days to request dispute resolution institutions in India like Indian Council of Arbitration  or  ICADR to nominate another arbitrator as above.
The language(s) of the arbitration shall be English. “Except as may be required by law, neither a party nor its representatives may disclose the existence, content, or results of any arbitration hereunder without the prior written consent of (all/both) parties.”
In case of technical disputes involving confidential matters, the issue shall be referred to a high level technical authority for each party, appointed for this purpose.
Clause for Defence Public Sector Undertakings or Public Sector Undertakings:
In the event of any dispute or difference relating to the interpretation and application of the provisions of commercial contract(s) between Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs)/ Port Trusts inter se and also between CPSEs and Government Departments/Organizations (excluding disputes concerning Railways, Income Tax, Customs &Excise Departments), such disputes or differences shall be taken up by either party for resolution through AMRCD as mentioned in DPE OM No.4(1)/2013-DPE(GM)/FTS-1835 dated 22-05-2018 as amended from time to time.

title: Obsolescence
body: The SUPPLIER shall continue to support the equipment for a minimum period of ___ years (equivalent to product support period) from the date of supply by making available spare parts and assemblies of the equipment supplied. For any reason SUPPLIER wishes / decides to close / discontinue the line for manufacture of the products or procurement of certain components, sub-components, SUPPLIER undertakes to notify such a decision to BUYER by means of a prior __ years notice (before closure of the said production line) in writing so as to enable BUYER to place buy order/a life time buy of all spares before closure of said production line. SUPPLIER will transfer tools, drawings etc., to BUYER after such notice period (free of charge). SUPPLIER shall indicate the source from where BUYER can procure these items. The said aspect would also form an integral part of the contract.

title: Work & Payment during Arbitration
body: Work under the Contract shall be continued by the SUPPLIER during the arbitration proceeding, unless otherwise directed in writing by the BUYER or unless the matter is such that the work cannot possibly be continued until the decision of the arbitrators is obtained, and save as those which are otherwise expressly provided in the Contract, no payment due or payable by the BUYER shall be withheld on account of such arbitration proceedings, unless it is the subject matter or one of the subject matters thereof.

title: Jurisdiction /Applicable laws
body:
The Court at Bangalore/place of Division only shall have jurisdiction to deal with and to decide any legal matter whatsoever arising out of this contract.
This contract shall be governed by and subject to and interpreted and construed in accordance with the Laws of Republic of India, which are in force from time to time.
Nothing in this contract shall entitle the Parties to this contract to exercise the rights, privilege and powers conferred under this contract in a manner which will contravene the Laws of India.

title: Change in Law and Regulations
body: If, after the  date twenty eight (28) days prior to the date of Bid submission or from the date of execution of the Contract in the country/place where the contract performance is required, any law, regulation, ordinance, order or By-Law having the force of Law is enacted, promulgated, abrogated or changed, which shall be deemed to include any change in interpretation or application by the competent authority/ies, that subsequently increase the costs and expenses of the SUPPLIER/OEM and/or the time for completion, the contract price shall be correspondingly increased or decreased and/or the time for completion shall be reasonably adjusted to the extent that the SUPPLIER/OEM has thereby been affected in the performance of any of its obligations under the contract.

title: Sub-contracting/ Sub-letting
body: SUPPLIER shall not be entitled without BUYER's prior written consent to Subcontract/ Sublet to a third party all or part of the benefits or obligations of the Contract (even by way of change of ownership or control), except as expressly permitted in this Contract if any, to sub-contract any of its rights and interest under this Contract.

title: Bribes
body:
The SUPPLIER undertakes that he has not given, offered or promised to give, directly or indirectly any gift, consideration, reward, commission, fees brokerage or inducement to any person in service of the BUYER or otherwise in procuring the Contract/s or forbearing to do or for having done or for borne to do any act in relation to the obtaining or execution of the Contract or any other Contract with the Government for showing or forbearing to show favour or disfavour to any person in relation to the Contract or any other Contract with the Government. Any breach of the aforesaid undertaking by the SUPPLIER or any one employed by him or acting on his behalf (whether with or without the knowledge of the SUPPLIER) or the commission of any offers by the SUPPLIER or anyone employed by him or acting on his behalf, as defined in Chapter IX of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 or the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 or any other Act enacted for the prevention of corruption shall entitle the BUYER to cancel the contract and all or any other contracts with the SUPPLIER and recover from the SUPPLIER the amount of any loss arising from such cancellation. A decision of the BUYER or his nominee to the effect that a breach of the undertaking had been committed shall be final and binding on the SUPPLIER.
Giving or offering of any gift, bribe or inducement or any attempt at any such act on behalf of the SUPPLIER towards any officer/employee of the BUYER or to any other person in a position to influence any officer/employee of the BUYER for showing any favour in relation to this or any other contract, shall render the SUPPLIER to such liability/ penalty as the BUYER may deem proper, including but not limited to termination of the contract, imposition of penal damages, forfeiture of the Bank Guarantee and refund of the amounts paid by the BUYER

title: Insolvency
body:
If the SUPPLIER enters into liquidation, whether compulsory or voluntary (other than amalgamation or reconstruction with another party taking over all its rights as well as commitments) or becomes insolvent or Suffers a receiver of the whole or part of its asset to be appointed,
Shall forthwith notify the same to BUYER and the BUYER shall have the right without prejudice to his other rights or remedies to terminate the unexecuted part of this Contract.
In such an event, the BUYER shall become entitled forthwith to get the refund within 30 days of all the advance payments received by the SUPPLIER and expenditure incurred by as a part of its obligations under this contract it has not fulfilled.
In such an event if applicable, the SUPPLIER is liable for return of any materials/items (including drawings, designs etc) to BUYER, which are held at his end as a part of the obligations under this contract.

title: Appropriation
body: Whenever under this contract any sum of money is due or recoverable from SUPPLIER or payable by the SUPPLIER, BUYER shall be entitled to recover such sum by appropriating in part or whole by deducting any sum then due or which at any time thereafter may become due to the SUPPLIER in this or any other contract entered by BUYER as a whole on behalf of its Divisions and Branch Offices etc., held by him alone or in partnership with others. Should this sum be not sufficient to cover the full amount recoverable, the SUPPLIER shall pay to BUYER on demand the remaining balance due within 30 days of such written notice? The remaining balance due, if any, will be recovered through due process of law in case SUPPLIER becomes defaulter.

title: Amendment & Waiver
body: Any amendment to Purchase Order / Contract would be enforceable only if made in writing and duly signed by authorized representatives of the parties hereto.  Failure of either Party at any time to enforce any of the provisions of this Contract shall not per se constitute a waiver by that Party of any such provisions nor in anyway affect the validity of the Contract or any part hereof.

title: Integrity Pact
body:
Bidder/s shall submit duly signed Integrity Pact in original, strictly as per the format (without any deviation) enclosed with the RFP. Bidder/s not complying with this is liable for rejection and their bids will not be considered for evaluation.
In case of two bid system, the Bidder is required to submit the signed pre-contract IP as part of technical bid, failing which offers are liable for rejection.

title: Relationship of the parties
body:
It is understood that each party is an independent party and that all persons engaged in the work under the Order that are supplied by either party shall in no sense be employees of the other party.
It is further agreed that neither party shall have the right to act as the agent or legal representative of the other party or to bind the other party in any respect whatsoever or to incur any debts or liabilities in the name or on behalf of the other party.

title: Acceptance of Services
body: BUYER/SERVICE RECIPIENT will inspect Services within 15 calendar days of written notice from SUPPLIER/SERVICE PROVIDER of completion of Services. Services will be presumed accepted unless SUPPLIER/SERVICE PROVIDER receives written notice of rejection explaining the basis for rejection within that time. SUPPLIER/SERVICE PROVIDER, at his option, will be afforded a reasonable opportunity to correct or re-perform the Services, rejected Services and provided the reason for rejection is due solely to the fault of SUPPLIER/SERVICE PROVIDER

title: Purchase Order/s
body: Orders will be governed by the terms of this Product/Services Conditions of Sale and may will specify: (i) SUPPLIER's Product part number with a general description of the Product/Service; (ii) requested delivery dates; (iii) applicable price; (iv) quantity; (v) location to which the Product is to be shipped; and (vi) location to which invoices will be sent for payment. Orders are subject to acceptance by SUPPLIER acknowledging the same within 10 working days from the date of receipt of the Purchase Order and if the SUPPLIER fails to acknowledge the same within the stipulated time, then the BUYER shall treat the Purchase order as deemed to be accepted by the SUPPLIER.

title: Waiver
body: Failure of either Party at any time to enforce any of the provisions of this Contract shall not per se constitute a waiver by that Party of any such provisions nor in anyway affect the validity of the Contract or any part hereof.

title: Severability
body: If any provision or portion of a provision of this Contract is determined to be illegal, invalid, or unenforceable, then that portion or provision will be stricken/treated invalid and the validity and enforceability of the remaining provisions will not be affected

title: Short-Closure of Contract
body:
BUYER reserve the right to short-close the contract with 02 months prior notice to the SUPPLIER at any time during the tenure of the contract. The liability of BUYER in this case will be limited to the extent of the cost as assessed by BUYER in its opinion, incurred by Vendor/SUPPLIER till the point of termination of contract.
BUYER shall reserve the right to short close this contract without giving justification or reasons for the same.
In the event of such short closure SUPPLIER shall immediately stop balance scope of work, subject to the terms of this Contract, SUPPLIER shall be paid the portion of the price reflecting the actual costs incurred for the part performance prior to the notice of short closure.  SUPPLIER shall make reasonably available to BUYER, any books, records and papers, other relevant documents supporting its claim. SUPPLIER shall not be paid for such scope of work supplied or costs incurred which should have been avoided. No indirect liabilities shall be entertained

title: Shelf Life
body: Where items offered have a limited shelf life, kindly indicate the life and confirm that such items shall have a minimum of 90% (or may be decided suitably based on type of item and duration of usage of material etc) of shelf life at the time of dispatch. In respect of rubber items such as Seals etc. having cure date, the item should not have been manufactured earlier than 6 months of date of dispatch.

title: Extension of Time
body:
The Time for Completion specified in the Contract shall be extended if the SUPPLIER has delayed or impeded in the performance of any of its obligations under the Contract by reason of any of the following:
Change as provided under (Change in the SOW), or
occurrence of Force Majeure as provided under (Force Majeure), or
adverse physical conditions, obstructions and pollutants encountered by the SUPPLIER at place of work, including sub-surface and hydrological conditions that could not have been reasonably foreseen prior to the date of the Contract by an experienced Vendor, or
changes in laws as intimated by the BUYER or
default or breach of the Contract by the BUYER, or any activity, act or omission of the BUYER or
delay attributable to the BUYER or caused by BUYER, or
any other matter specifically mentioned in the Contract
by such period as shall be fair and reasonable in all the circumstances and as shall fairly reflect the delay or impediment sustained by the SUPPLIER, subject to acceptance by the BUYER.

title: Immunity to the Government of India
body: It is expressly understood and agreed by and between SUPPLIER&BUYER that BUYER is entering into this contact solely on its own behalf and not on behalf of any other person or entity. In particular, it is expressly understood and agreed that Government of India is not a party to this contract and has no liabilities, obligations or right hereunder. It is expressly understood and agreed that BUYER is an independent legal entity with power and authority to enter into contracts solely on its own behalf under the applicable laws of India and general principles of contract law. SUPPLIER expressly agrees, acknowledge and understand that BUYER is not an agent, representative or delegate to the Government of India. It is further agreed and understood that Government of India is not and shall not be liable for any acts, omissions, commissions, breaches or other wrongs arising out of the contract. Accordingly, SUPPLIER hereby expressly waives releases and foregoes any and all actions, including counterclaims, implied claims or counter claims against the Government of India arising out of this contract and covenants not to sue the Government of India as to any manner, claim cause of action or thing whatsoever arising out of or under this contract.

title: Access to Books of Accounts
body: In case it is found to the satisfaction of the BUYER that the Bidder/Supplier has engaged an Agent or paid commission or influenced any person to obtain the contract as described in clauses relating to Agents/Agency Commission and penalty for use of undue influence, the Bidder/Supplier, on a specific request of the BUYER, shall provide necessary information/ inspection of the relevant financial documents/ information.

title: Cartel Formation
body:
Cartel formation or quoting of pool rates or quoting in collusion is against the basic principle of competitive bidding and shall attract penal and punitive measures; including blacklisting of such Bidders either permanently or for a specified period, apart from reporting to the Competition Commission of India, other Regulatory Authorities, Chambers/ Associations of Commerce, etc.
a) Firms are expected to quote for full quantity or part thereof but not less than ___% of tendered quantity. Offers for quantity less than ___% of tendered quantity will be considered unresponsive and liable to be rejected if CARTEL Formation is suspected. The parties to the contract                                                              , reserves the right to order any quantity on one or more firms.
b) Wherever all or most of the approved firms quote equal rates in CARTEL, the purchaser reserves the right to place order on any one or more firms with exclusion of the rest. The selection of firms for placement of order would be based on of a pre-determined ranking of the firms as per RFP evaluation criteria.
c) The purchaser reserves the right to place order on two or three firms: in such cases tender quantity will be distributed between Rank 1(R1) and rank 2(R2) firms in the ratio 60:40 or among R1, R2 and Rank 3(R3) firms in the ratios 50:30:20 respectively or award contract to vendor who is offering better commercial terms. BUYER needs to decide on splitting of tender quantity  (when more than one vendor offers at same rate and considered that it is not a cartel formation and no such conditions wrt splitting are part of RFP) considering facts like technicality of whether tendered item can be purchased from different vendors , other vendors agrees to supply part quantity etc.
d) The purchaser reserves the right to delete the registered firms who quote in CARTEL from list of approved/registered sources or to debar them from competing for a period to be decided by the purchaser.
e) The name of the newly registered firm which enters into CARTEL on getting registered will be summarily deleted from the list of registered SUPPLIERs.
f) New firms will have to submit an undertaking that they will not be part of a cartel with other vendors and will quote competitive rates in the tenders; otherwise would face expulsion from the list of vendor.

title: Latent Defects Liability
body:
If any latent defect shall appear in any part of the Stores or works, supplied or done, within a period of 5 years after the completion of the warranty period the same shall be made good by the SUPPLIER/Executant, provided that:
the defect was caused by a negligent act or omission on the part of the SUPPLIER/Executant and
would not have been disclosed by a reasonable examination prior to the expiry of the respective warranty period, this include manufacturing defect.

title: Limitation of Liability
body: Notwithstanding any other provisions of this Contract, except in cases of Criminal negligence or wilful misconduct, the aggregate liability of the SUPPLIER to the BUYER, whether under the contract, in tort or otherwise, shall be to the actual loss or damage caused/suffered by BUYER directly or indirectly, provided that this limitation shall not apply to the cost of repairing and replacing defective equipment.

title: Exclusion of Consequential Losses
body: Notwithstanding any other provision of this Contract, except in cases of gross negligence or wilful misconduct, neither party shall be liable to the other party, whether in contract, tort or otherwise, for loss of use, loss of production, loss of contract, loss of opportunity or loss of profits or interest costs, which may be suffered by the other Party in connection with the contract or for any indirect or consequential loss or damage, other than specifically provided as an obligation of the Party in the contract.

title: Priority of Documents
body:
The following documents shall constitute the Contract between the BUYER and the SUPPLIER, each document shall be read and construed as an integral part of the contract:
(a) (….document details to be written…)
(b)(….document details to be written…)

In the event of any ambiguity or conflict between the contract documents listed above, the order of the priority shall be the order in which the contract documents are listed above.
Specific terms agreed take priority over the general statement and in the same group of the contract documents created at later date govern over earlier contract documents.

title: Entire Agreement
body: This Contract/Purchase order contains the entire agreement between the parties with respect to the subject matter of this Contract/Order and supersedes any prior representations or agreements, oral or written, and all other communications between the parties relating to the subject matter of this Contract/ Purchase Order. This Contract/Purchase Order will not be varied except in writing signed by an authorized representative of each Party.

title: Agency/Partnership
body: Nothing in this Contract/Agreement shall create, or be deemed to create, a joint venture, partnership or the relationship of principal and agent between the parties.  Except as expressly authorised in this Contract/Agreement, neither party has any authority to act, make representations or bind or contract on behalf of the other party.

title: Non-Assignment
body: Neither of the parties to this contract shall be entitled without the other party's consent to assign or transfer to a third party all or a part of the benefits or obligations of this contract, subject to such consent not to be unreasonably withheld by the party to whom it is sought.

title: Sufficiency
body:
The OEMs have to ensure that the depth of Technology being transferred shall enable the Production/Manufacturing Agency achieve value addition commensurate with a minimum __ % of the relative cost of the licensed Product through indigenous manufacture in case of ________ based on ToT and a minimum of ____% of the relative cost of the licensed product through indigenous manufacture in case of _______ based ToT (100% self-sufficiency in the manufacture of spares, modules, systems, sub-system etc. which are required for the repair/ maintenance activities for _____ and ____ level servicing on long term basis for the Aircraft, its engine, role equipment, accessories, systems etc., is desired. The OEM should commit to transfer of a depth of technology which would ensure that the indigenous content of production with respect to the total production cost in India should be to the extent indicated above).
In the event of any deficiencies observed in the ability of the test equipment to perform the ATP and the content of the data required to perform the repairs/manufacture/usage, such deficiencies shall be corrected free of charge.
SUPPLIER/OEM declares and warrants to BUYER that it is competent and has all the know-how, capability, expertise, means, personnel and facilities to perform the tasks specified in this contract in a proper, timely, complete and workmanlike manner using proper materials and engineering practice.

title: Protective Clause
body:
The BUYER/CUSTOMER undertakes to use any property, Experimental Models, Documentation, results of works and services performed by the OEM/SUPPLIER, which are supplied under the present Contract for the declared purposes only. BUYER/CUSTOMER should develop a robust system to control access to information contained in these deliverables to only personnel authorized by it.
BUYER/CUSTOMER will be able to either formally or actually to re-export or deliver any property, Experimental Models, Documentation, results of works and services performed by the OEM/SUPPLIER, which are supplied under the present Contract or any information about them to the third countries or to any physical persons or legal entities from those countries in case of obtaining a formal consent of the OEM/SUPPLIER Country only which is issued by the OEM/SUPPLIER upon receipt of the appropriate written request from BUYER/CUSTOMER according to the legislation of the OEM/SUPPLIER Country. BUYER/CUSTOMER shall ensure protection of the information received during execution of the present Contract.
BUYER/CUSTOMER shall not without prior consent of the OEM/SUPPLIER;
Replicate, re-engineer or reproduce any property supplied by the Company under the present Contract including Experimental Models, Documentation.
Use any OEM/SUPPLIER inventions, “know-how” and other results of scientific research and development other than for the purpose of implementation of the Contract and purposes agreed in the Contract.
Modify or improve any property supplied under the present Contract.
In case the property is to be modified by BUYER/CUSTOMER during R&D in compliance with above requirements, the OEM/SUPPLIER is granted preferential right to accomplish works to modify the property. The OEM/SUPPLIER will propose possible options for the property modification.
The provisions of this clause will apply reciprocally to the OEM/SUPPLIER also wherever context so demands.

title: Indemnity (Third Party indemnity)
body:
The SUPPLIER shall indemnify and hold harmless the BUYER and its Affiliates and their respective officers, partners, directors and employees, or any of them, and their successors and assigns, from and against any and all liabilities, damages, losses, claims, demands actions, causes, of action and costs (including reasonable attorneys fee and expenses) for any Third Party claims relating to property damage and or bodily injury to the extent caused directly by negligence of the SUPPLIER.
The SUPPLIER shall have sole authority for the control of the defence of any and all such Third Party claims and suits brought thereon, and the BUYER shall render such assistance as the SUPPLIER may reasonably require in connection therewith, provided that in any suit brought on any claim, the BUYER shall have the right to be represented by counsel of its own choice and at its own expense.
The BUYER shall indemnify and hold harmless the SUPPLIER and its Affiliates and their respective officers, partners, directors and employees, or any of them, and their successors and assigns, from and against any and all liabilities, damages, losses, claims, demands, actions, causes of action and costs (including reasonable attorney’s fees and expenses) for any Third Party claims relating to property damages and or bodily injury to the extent caused directly by the negligence of the BUYER.

body: All correspondence between the parties, as well as all documentation, manuals, software listings and other writings, in connection with this Contract shall be in the English

title: Counter Parts
body: This Agreement/Contract shall be executed in two or more number of counterparts depending upon the number of Parties and each fully executed Counterpart shall be deemed to be original.

title: Risk Purchase
body:
In the event that the SUPPLIER fails to deliver the Deliverables within ______ days following the conclusion of the period prescribed for such delivery under
Clause _____/Annexure __ (may specify the delivery schedule), the BUYER may purchase the deliverables which are undelivered from other sources and such a replacement total cost to the BUYER for such item, shall be deducted by the BUYER from the next upcoming payment or payments to be made to SUPPLIER or SUPPLIER to make payment of such amounts to BUYER. Claim to be forwarded by BUYER to SUPPLIER in this regard.

title: Defect Investigation
body:
When the supplied item is within the warranty period and the defect being confirmed by the SUPPLIER on notification issued by BUYER, the defective item will be sent to SUPPLIER at his cost for defect investigation and return, free of cost.
When the supplied item is outside the warranty period, BUYER will advise the SUPPLIER the nature of defect and seek advice to set right the defect, if it is minor in nature. Otherwise on the advice of the SUPPLIER, defective component/unit shall be dispatched for Defect Investigation (DI) and rectification. The defect investigation should be carried out and the defect investigation report should be forwarded within 30 days from the date of receipt of defective component/unit. Expenditure towards To & Fro dispatch, insurance, applicable taxes/charges and rectification subject to prior approval from SUPPLIER will be borne by BUYER.
In case of the defect investigation report states that the defect is due to manufacturing defect, then the SUPPLIER shall be responsible for the entire cost of rectification, including to and fro freight, applicable taxes/charges, insurance etc.
A commitment is to be provided to undertake defect investigation and repair/overhaul, till the facilities are set up in BUYER. Cost of DI / ROH is also to be quoted in the offer.
The SUPPLIER should complete the defect investigation (DI) and forward the DI Reports to BUYER by e-mail/fax within 30 days of receipt of the defective item by them. If the item is repairable, the same should be completed in another 30 (thirty) days or as per mutually agreed period and dispatched to BUYER by the fastest means.
If not repairable, the replacement item should be sent to BUYER depending on the terms of the Purchase Order/warranty conditions. Even if the item is not repairable, defect investigation should be carried out by the SUPPLIER and a report forwarded to BUYER.
The investigation report must also give details of the bench check/Functional checks carried out, results of strip examinations to bring out the root cause of the malfunction/failure and what the SUPPLIER intends to do to remedy the malfunction / failure. Details of the work content that is required to be carried out by the SUPPLIER and the outline of the kind of report expected shall be indicated in the initial communication by BUYER to the SUPPLIER and before SUPPLIER takes the defective item for investigation.
The SUPPLIER should particularly note that Defect Investigation requirement is the prerogative of BUYER and the SUPPLIER is required to complete the DI and send the repaired/new item along with the DI report. While making necessary improvements in the supplied product, depending on field failures, the SUPPLIER must indicate the improvements incorporated and supply the new/upgraded product to higher drawing issue without additional charges (including future supplies if any).
Any retro modifications in already supplied goods/replacement of defective goods to be done free of charge (even after expiry of warranty period), if defect is traceable to inherent design and manufacturing defects.

title: Firm Prices
body: The contract prices will be firm and fixed as per contract terms till execution of contract and exclude subsequent claims or price increases of any kind including for the extended contract period.

title: Non Exclusivity
body: Nothing herein is intended nor shall be construed as creating any exclusion arrangement with SUPPLIER/Service Provider/Executants. This contract shall not restrict the BUYER/Service Recipient/Customer from acquiring same/similar goods and /or services from other entities or services.

title: Agents & Agency Commission
body: The seller confirms and declares to the buyer that the seller is the original manufacturer or authorized distributor / stockist of original manufacturer or Govt. Sponsored / Designated Export Agencies (applicable in case of countries where domestic laws do not permit direct export by OEMS) of the stores referred to in this offer / contract / Purchase order and has not engaged any individual or firm, whether Indian or Foreign whatsoever, to intercede, facilitate or in any way to recommend to Buyer or any of its functionaries, whether officially or unofficially, to the award of the contract / purchase order to the Seller; nor has any amount been paid, promised or intended to be paid to any such individual or firm in respect of any such intercession, facilitation or recommendation. The Seller agrees that if it is established at any time to the satisfaction of the Buyer that the present declaration is in any way incorrect or if at a later stage it is discovered by the Buyer that the Seller has engaged any such individual / firm, and paid or intended to pay any amount, gift, reward, fees, commission or consideration to such person, party, firm or institution, whether before or after the signing of this contract / purchase order, the Seller will be liable to refund that amount to the Buyer. The Seller will also be debarred from participating in any RFQ / Tender for new projects / program with Buyer for a minimum period of five years. The Buyer will also have a right to consider cancellation of the Contract / Purchase order either wholly or in part, without any entitlement or compensation to the Seller who shall in such event be liable to refund all payments made by the Buyer in terms of the Contract / Purchase order along with interest at the rate of 2% per annum above LIBOR (London Inter Bank Offer Rate) (for foreign vendors) and Base Rate of SBI (State Bank of India) plus 2% (for Indian vendors). The Buyer will also have the right to recover any such amount from any contracts / Purchase order concluded earlier with Buyer.

title: Payment Terms
body: Both the Parties herein agree that the term of payment shall be made 100% within 30 days of supply, inspection, receipt and acceptance at HAL Stores/services, by RTGS or any other latest Electronic Payment remittance mode, subject to Seller/Vendor providing all required documents/upon fulfillment of Supplier’s supply obligations under contract etc.

title: Right to reject Proposal
body:
Notwithstanding anything contained in this RFP, the Authority reserves the right to accept or reject any Proposal and to annul the Selection Process and reject all Proposals, at any time without any liability or any obligation for such acceptance, rejection or annulment, and without assigning any reasons therefore.
Without prejudice to the generality in the tender terms, the Authority reserves the right to reject any Proposal if:
(a) at any time, a material misrepresentation is made or discovered, or
(b) the Bidder does not provide, within the time specified by the Authority, the supplemental information sought by the Authority for evaluation of the Proposal.
Misrepresentation/ improper response by the Bidder may lead to the disqualification of the Bidder. If the Bidder is the Lead Member of a consortium, then the entire consortium may be disqualified / rejected. If such disqualification / rejection occurs after the Proposals have been opened and the highest ranking Bidder gets disqualified / rejected, then the Authority reserves the right to consider the next best Bidder, or take any other measure as may be deemed fit in the sole discretion of the Authority, including annulment of the Tender Process.

title: Supply of Alternative Item
body: In case if the bidder is quoting for an alternative part number it should be confirmed that the offered part is fully interchangeable with the required part. Applicable descriptive literature/catalogue if any may please be enclosed by the bidder with offer.

title: Counterfeit Parts
body:
Seller represents and warrants that it has policies and procedures in place to ensure that none of the supplies or materials furnished under this Purchase Order/contract are “counterfeit parts” and certifies, to the best of its knowledge and belief that no such parts have been or are being furnished to Buyer by Seller. “Counterfeit parts” are parts that may be of new manufacture, but are misleadingly labelled to provide the impression they are of a different class or quality or from a different source than is actually the case. They also include refurbished parts, complete with false labelling, that are represented as new parts or any parts that are designated as counterfeit by any Government/Authority under control, and If Buyer reasonably determines that Seller has supplied counterfeit parts to Buyer, Buyer shall promptly notify Seller and Seller shall immediately replace the counterfeit parts with parts acceptable to Buyer.
Notwithstanding any other provision contained herein, Seller shall be liable for all costs incurred by Buyer to remove and replace the counterfeit parts, including without limitation to any loss/damage in part/full to Aircraft caused due to such counterfeit part and Buyer’s external and internal costs of removing such a counterfeit parts, of reinserting replacement parts and of any testing necessitated by the reinstallation of Seller’s goods after counterfeit parts have been exchanged and third party liabilities if any . In addition, Buyer may unilaterally terminate this order for Convenience depending on the impact of the delivery of Counterfeit parts on the Seller’s overall performance on this order. Seller’s warranty against counterfeit parts shall survive any termination or expiration of this Purchase Order/Contract. Buyer reserves the right to seize and quarantine any / all counterfeit products it receives from Seller on this Purchase Order/Contract. Counterfeit products may be forwarded to the Original Component Manufacturer and / or the appropriate authority for final analysis, possible confiscation and / or destruction. If products furnished by the Seller are determined to in fact be counterfeit, Seller agrees to reimburse Buyer on the full purchase price paid as well as any shipping or third party testing charges incurred by Buyer. Further the Buyer reserves the right to ban the Seller thereafter for such period as deemed appropriate.

title: Rights of Sale and Utilisation – Export License/Re-Export Permission
body:
1.1 As the requirement is for Military/Civil application, a specific confirmation from Bidders/Sellers on availability of export license from their respective Government should be provided and a copy of such relevant permission / license issued should be enclosed.
1.2 Bidders /Suppliers shall be required to obtain and maintain all Export/Import licences and permits etc., as the case may be, required for performing supplies against this tender. Obtaining export licence and timely availability shall be entire/sole responsibility of the Bidders/Suppliers, which forms a part of obligations of the contract. However any unforeseen delay should be promptly informed to HAL with proper justification.
If End user certificate is required from HAL, the format of the same may be enclosed with this offer.
1.3 Bidders/Suppliers may indicate status of export permit based on the present rules/ regulations of their respective country and normal time frame for obtaining such export permission if an order is placed in near future and the said time frame should be covered within the delivery schedule indicated.
1.4 Bidders/Suppliers should also confirm that necessary clearances are available/will be made available from their Governmental authorities regarding the sharing of technical data required for integration purposes with other vendors of Aircraft /Helicopter on a need to know basis.
1.5 Clearance in unequivocal terms also needs to be accorded regarding export of the equipment fitted as a part of the military and civil variant Aircraft /Helicopters, spare LRUs, modules & components and service support when such activities are undertaken by HAL India to other countries. Reservations if any may be specifically indicated as a part of the Bid.
1.6 Bidders/Suppliers to confirm that there are no restrictions for exporting HAL Aircraft/helicopters to any country, fitted with the LRU/Systems/items offered/supplied by them.
1.7 Buyer (HAL) will have exclusive worldwide sale and support right for all supplies under contract if specifically developed and funded by HAL. Any enquiry received on such equipment shall be directed to Buyer and Bidder/Seller will not directly sell / support / service without prior concurrence of Buyer. For all development orders all the Intellectual Proprietary Rights (IPR) will rest with Buyer.
1.8 The prices to be quoted by Bidders/Sellers for exports should be competitive in international market scenario.
1.9 In case of grant of Rights for Transfer of Technology (ToT) to Buyer for manufacture and/ or Repair and Overhaul (RoH), then Buyer will have exclusive rights for worldwide sale of the Aircraft / Helicopter incorporating the items manufactured/ Repaired & Overhauled under ToT.
